title: Getting CVX-4210 during traffic spikes — how to stop it?

posts.author: tom_b
posts.body: Every morning when our batch import kicks off we get a wave of `CVX-4210 enqueue rejected: queue depth limit reached` and jobs get dropped on the floor. How do we make it stop rejecting?

posts.author: quickfix_carl
posts.body: Just disable the limit. Set `queue.max_depth: 0` in corvex.yaml and it'll never reject again. Been running like that for months.

posts.author: priya_corvex
posts.body:
Please don't do that. On Corvex 2.x `queue.max_depth: 0` means 'reject every enqueue', not 'unbounded' — if that config isn't rejecting for you, something else is going on (maybe you're still on 1.x semantics, or the key isn't being read). 'Unbounded' is `-1`, and it's dangerous without alerting because a stuck consumer will OOM your Redis.

The right fix for a predictable morning spike: (1) add worker capacity for that window, or (2) raise `queue.max_depth` to roughly 1.5× your expected peak backlog and make sure Redis has the memory, or (3) enqueue the batch onto a dedicated lower-priority queue so it can't starve real-time work. CVX-4210 is backpressure doing its job — the goal is to drain faster, not to remove the safety valve.

posts.author: tom_b
posts.body: Moved the import to its own `bulk` queue with 2 extra workers during that window. No more 4210. Thanks.
